claims.text: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi can be prepared as a single-phase FCC solid solution.
The initial HEA has no significant pre-existing grain-boundary segregation, nanoclusters, or intermetallic precipitates.
High-strain-rate deformation can cause brittle behavior in an initially single-phase HEA through dynamic grain-boundary nanoclustering.
The proposed brittle behavior is not caused by pre-existing equilibrium grain-boundary precipitates or impurity segregation.
High-strain-rate sliding or shear can produce highly localized, shear-induced severe plastic deformation in CoCrFeMnNi.
Ultra-high-vacuum, low-thermal-load testing minimizes oxidation and thermally activated diffusion effects.
High-strain-rate deformation dynamically clusters principal elements at high-angle grain boundaries.
Cr, Ni, and Mn are among the elements expected to form the dynamic grain-boundary nanoclusters.
Dynamic grain-boundary nanoclustering reduces grain-boundary cohesive strength.
Reduced grain-boundary cohesion caused by nanoclustering promotes cavitation or nanoscale porosity.
Grain-boundary cavities nucleate intergranular cracks and brittle fracture.
In conventional metals and alloys, impurity segregation at grain boundaries can weaken boundary strength and promote grain-boundary crack initiation.
Second-phase precipitation at grain boundaries can create deformation-incompatibility stress concentrations that promote crack initiation.
Relative to a low-strain-rate control, high-strain-rate deformation will produce greater nanoscale compositional fluctuations at grain boundaries.
Relative to a low-strain-rate control, high-strain-rate deformation will increase grain-boundary nanoporosity.
Relative to a low-strain-rate control, high-strain-rate deformation will reduce toughness and cause earlier intergranular cracking.
The proposed mechanism is limited to high-strain-rate, low-thermal-load conditions and may cease to govern when thermal diffusion or impurity-driven segregation becomes significant.
